help_watch_info_q: How do I see a stream's resolution and codec?
help_watch_info_a:
Turn on Settings → Playback → Show stream information. When you change channels, a small banner shows the picture size, frame rate and codecs, and the channel list keeps a short technical line for every channel you have played – so you can see which are in HD before you open them.

For everything at once while something plays, press I for the playback stats. With Nerd on, Settings → Nerd → Diagnostics → Stats for nerds adds more to them.

Nothing is remembered during private viewing.
help_places_tv_q: What does the TV place show?
help_places_tv_a:
TV in the sidebar lists the channels of the category you pick on the left: number, logo, what is on now with a bar for how far it has got, and what comes next. The channel that plays is marked Playing.

  • Recently watched at the top brings back the channels you watched last. Right-click its heading → Hide this row if you do not want it.
  • The sort button in the header orders the category the way you like, or as the provider sends it.
  • Compact fits more channels on the screen; Airy gives each one more room and a bigger logo.
  • A name too long for its column shows in full when you hold the pointer over it.

Click a channel to play it. Right-click it for favourites, recording, reminders, hiding and renaming.
help_places_films_q: How do I browse movies and series?
help_places_films_a:
Movies and Series in the sidebar show the category you pick on the left, as posters or as a list – the switch is in the header, and your choice is remembered.

  • Popular right now at the top is this week's chart from TMDB, matched to what your provider actually has.
  • Continue holds what you have started: one click goes on from where you stopped.
  • Click a film to see it in the column on the right; double-click it or press Enter to play it.
  • A series opens on its own page with its seasons and episodes.

Type in the filter field to narrow the list, and use the sort button to order the category. Popular right now can be turned off under Settings → Posters & info, or with Hide this row on its heading.
help_places_details_q: Where do the plot, rating and cast come from – and can I fix a wrong match?
help_places_details_a:
When you pick a film or a series, the column on the right shows its poster, plot, year, length, rating, genres and who is in it. What the provider lacks, dopeIPTV fills in from TMDB – asked with the title and year only, never your logins.

Wrong poster or plot? Right-click the title → Match on TMDB… and pick the right one. To use only your provider's own pictures and text, choose Provider artwork under Settings → Posters & info.
help_places_favs_q: How do favourites and folders work?
help_places_favs_a:
Right-click a channel, film or series → Add to favorites, or Add to folder to put it in a folder of your own (New folder… makes one). Your favourites are in Mine; favourite channels also show in TV mode and on the phone remote.

  • Under Mine → Favorite folders you rename, colour, lock and remove folders, drag titles into the order you want, and drop a title on another folder to move it there.
  • A locked folder asks for the parental PIN, and a kids profile never sees it.
  • Favourites are kept per source and per profile, and follow you to your other computers with sync.
help_guide_reminders_q: How do I get a reminder when a programme starts?
help_guide_reminders_a:
Right-click a programme that has not started yet – in the guide, or among what comes next on a channel – and choose Remind me when it starts. When it begins, dopeIPTV tells you, with Watch now to switch to it.

All your reminders are under File → Reminders…, where you can remove them. For every airing of a programme, use a series rule instead: Record series… → Remind me.

File → Export to calendar… saves your reminders and scheduled recordings as a calendar file. With the phone remote or the remote API turned on, a calendar app on your home network can subscribe to them instead and stay up to date by itself.
help_guide_seriesrec_q: Can I record every episode of a series automatically?
help_guide_seriesrec_a:
Yes. Right-click a programme in the guide → Record series… and choose:

  • Record or Remind me,
  • the exact title, or a word in it,
  • this channel only, or any channel.

dopeIPTV looks through the guide for every airing and adds the recordings with your padding (Settings → Recording → Padding). It never records the same programme twice – nor one shown on two channels at once – and a recording you cancel is not scheduled again.

Your rules are under Settings → Recording → Series recordings. On an Enigma2 box with AutoTimer you can let the box keep the rule itself, so it records even while your computer is off.
help_guide_mp4_q: Can recordings be saved as MP4?
help_guide_mp4_a:
Yes. Turn on Settings → Recording → Save recordings as MP4. When a recording is finished, dopeIPTV copies it into an MP4 that plays on phones, TVs and in any player. Nothing is re-encoded, so it takes a moment and the quality stays exactly the same.

The original .ts file is deleted only once the MP4 has been checked and is whole. With Keep teletext and subtitles on, a recording that has teletext or DVB subtitles stays a .ts – an MP4 cannot carry them.
help_sources_find_q: Can dopeIPTV find my box or media server by itself?
help_sources_find_a:
Yes. When you add a source under Settings → Sources, press Find on my network. dopeIPTV looks on your home network for boxes and servers – HDHomeRun tuners, SAT>IP servers, Enigma2 boxes, Tvheadend, VDR, DVBViewer, NextPVR, MythTV, Jellyfin, Emby and Plex – and lists what it finds. Pick one and its address is filled in.

Press it again to stop. Found nothing? A network split into parts – VLANs, a separate network for the TV – hides what is on the other side: add those parts under Settings → Nerd → Network → Other networks (VLANs), or type the address yourself.
help_sources_e2_q: What can I do with an Enigma2 box from the app?
help_sources_e2_a:
Add the box as a source – VU+, Dreambox, Zgemma and other boxes with OpenWebif. Then right-click any of its channels → The box:

  • Show this channel on the box, Wake the box, Put the box to standby,
  • Box info… with its tuners and the live signal,
  • Screenshot from the box… of what its TV shows,
  • Remote control… with the box's own keys,
  • Edit the box's channel lists… – its bouquets.

The box's recordings are under Movies, in Recordings on the box: play them, or right-click → On the box to rename, move or delete them. dopeIPTV also counts the box's tuners and asks before something would cut off a recording on the box or what its TV shows.
help_cast_dlna_q: Can I cast to a smart TV or to Kodi?
help_cast_dlna_a:
Yes. Right-click → Cast to TV… lists smart TVs that speak DLNA/UPnP – Samsung, LG, Sony, Philips, Panasonic and many more – and Kodi, beside the Chromecasts.

  • Kodi: in Kodi, turn on Settings › Services › Control › Allow remote control via HTTP. If Kodi wants a user name and password, add it with Add Kodi… in the cast window.
  • Not in the list? Use Add a device by address… – handy when the TV is on another part of your network.

A TV and Kodi play the stream as it is; choosing audio, subtitles or picture size while casting works with a Chromecast.
help_cast_mediakeys_q: Do the media keys and the lock screen controls work?
help_cast_mediakeys_a:
Yes. dopeIPTV shows what plays in your system's own media controls – MPRIS on Linux (KDE Connect too), Now Playing on macOS, and on Windows the media controls by the volume and on the lock screen – and answers the keyboard's media keys and headphone buttons: play/pause, and next or previous channel or episode.

It is on from the start; the switch is under Settings → General → System. While you cast, the keys control the TV instead.
help_cast_outside_q: Can I start a channel from a script, a shortcut or a link?
help_cast_outside_a:
Yes – from the command line, a desktop shortcut, a script or a link on a web page:

dopeiptv --channel "My Channel"
dopeiptv --play https://example.com/live.m3u8
dopeiptv --tv

--channel plays a channel of the source in use by its name, --play a stream or a file, and --tv opens TV mode. A dopeiptv:// link does the same from a browser: dopeiptv://channel/My%20Channel, dopeiptv://play?url=… (a stream, never a file) or dopeiptv://open.

When dopeIPTV is already running, the command goes to that window instead of starting a second copy.
help_personal_backup_q: How do I back up my settings, or move them to a new computer?
help_personal_backup_a:
Settings → General → Backup → Back up… saves everything you would miss in one file: your sources with their logins, favourites, history, reminders, channel numbers, every profile and your settings. Caches and where the windows sit are left out.

Restore… shows what the file holds and lets you choose: put it back over everything (done the next time the app starts), or only add its sources beside the ones you have.

The file holds your logins – keep it somewhere safe. To keep two computers the same all the time, sync is easier.
help_personal_themes_q: Can I change how the app looks?
help_personal_themes_a:
Yes, under Settings → Appearance:

  • 25 themes, light and dark, and any Accent color,
  • Follow the desktop's light and dark mode – one theme by day, another by night,
  • Size of text and controls, and how round the corners are,
  • What the places show: take places out of the sidebar, hide the rows over the lists, or choose Just the list.

Each profile keeps its own look. Supporters get two extra themes.
help_personal_discord_q: Can Discord show what I am watching?
help_personal_discord_a:
Yes. Turn on Settings → Integrations → Discord → Show what I watch in Discord. While the Discord app runs on the same computer, your status says what plays and for how long. Under What it says you choose the channel, film or episode – or only “Watching TV”.

Nothing is shown during private viewing, and what plays then is not shown afterwards either.
help_privacy_private_q: Can I watch without it being remembered?
help_privacy_private_a:
Yes. History → Private viewing turns it on until the app closes: nothing you watch goes into History, Continue watching or your statistics, nothing goes to Trakt or Simkl, and Discord shows nothing. A mark in the sidebar shows that it is on.

History → Clear recent history removes what you watched in the last hour, three hours, day or five days – or all of it – for every source, your statistics included.
help_privacy_feedback_q: How do I send feedback or report a bug?
help_privacy_feedback_a:
In the app: Help → Send feedback. Before anything is sent you see the whole message exactly as it will go, with addresses, logins and anything else that could identify you taken out. Tick Show an answer to this in the app and the answer comes back under Help → Answers to feedback – no e-mail, no account.

After an error or a crash, dopeIPTV offers to send a report the same way. While a video plays, the offer waits in the menu.
help_nerd_what_a:
Extra settings for enthusiasts: boxes and servers at home, how the app talks to the network, and the player all the way down to mpv. None of it is needed to watch TV.

Turn it on under Settings → Nerd → Status → Nerd mode. Five pages appear – Network, Boxes and lists, Player, Remote and automation and Diagnostics – and each source's page gets its own Nerd options. Every setting is tried for real and says ✓, ! or ✗, with what is wrong.

Turned off, none of it applies – and what you set is kept for next time.
help_nerd_network_q: Can I set my own user agent, proxy or DNS?
help_nerd_network_a:
Yes, with Nerd on, under Settings → Nerd → Network:

  • Who the app says it is: user agent, referer and extra headers,
  • Proxy – for the player too, if you like,
  • Connection: IPv4 or IPv6, timeouts and reconnects,
  • Own DNS over HTTPS – Cloudflare, Quad9, Google or your own,
  • VPN guard, so nothing plays while the VPN is down,
  • Other networks (VLANs) to look for boxes on.

A source can have settings of its own: open it under Settings → Sources and use its Network tab. There you can also trust one certificate for a server whose own is not accepted.
help_nerd_mirrors_q: My provider has several server addresses – can the app switch by itself?
help_nerd_mirrors_a:
Yes. Open the source under Settings → Sources and, on its Network tab, put the other addresses in Backup addresses, one per line. While the one in use cannot be reached, the next one is tried – and kept. A wrong password or a missing channel never makes it switch.

Failover goes further: turn on Settings → Nerd → Boxes and lists → Try the channel in another source. A channel that will not play is then looked for in your other sources – by its guide id, else by its name – and played from there.
help_nerd_chno_q: Can I give the channels numbers of my own?
help_nerd_chno_a:
Yes, with Nerd on. Right-click a channel → Set channel number…, or number them all at once under Settings → Nerd → Boxes and lists → Channel numbers. Your numbers replace the provider's everywhere – the lists, the guide, TV mode and what you share with other players – and typing a number zaps to that channel.

With Nerd off, the provider's numbers are back; yours are kept for when it is on again.
help_nerd_player_q: How do I tune the player – low latency, mpv, a channel's own settings?
help_nerd_player_a:
With Nerd on, Settings → Nerd → Player has:

  • Low latency for live – closer to the broadcast, with a smaller buffer,
  • how a channel starts and how much it buffers,
  • the highest quality adaptive (HLS) streams may use,
  • audio passthrough, video sync and interpolation,
  • your own mpv options, mpv folder and shaders.

One channel can have its own audio and subtitle language, deinterlacing, aspect ratio and audio delay: right-click it → Channel settings….
help_nerd_api_q: Can I control dopeIPTV from Home Assistant or other devices?
help_nerd_api_a:
Yes, with Nerd on, under Settings → Nerd → Remote and automation:

  • Remote control over HTTP – a small API with a token, for this computer or your home network,
  • Publish events over MQTT, with Home Assistant's discovery and, if you allow it, its commands back: play, pause, volume, favourites and TV mode,
  • Webhooks – a POST to your addresses when something starts, stops or records,
  • Share with other players – all your channels as one M3U and the guides as one XMLTV,
  • Server for the home – dopeIPTV as a tuner for Plex, Jellyfin and Emby, and a playlist for VLC and Kodi.

During private viewing they hear what happened, never what you watched.
help_nerd_health_q: How do I find out why a channel keeps dropping?
help_nerd_health_a:
With Nerd on, turn on Settings → Nerd → Diagnostics → Keep stream health per channel. For every channel dopeIPTV then notes how often it starts, fails and drops, how long it takes to show a picture, and the last error. Channels with trouble get a dot in the list; right-click → Stream health… shows the details, and the Diagnostics page lists the worst ones.

To look at the stream itself, open Stream analysis… in the player's options menu while a live channel plays: a TR 101 290 check of sync, continuity errors, PCR timing and the bitrate of each stream in it. It reads dopeIPTV's own buffer (Rewind with dopeIPTV's own buffer under Settings → Playback), so it needs that turned on – and it never opens a second connection.
help_nerd_conntest_q: How do I test the connection to my provider step by step?
help_nerd_conntest_a:
With Nerd on, open the source under Settings → Sources and press Test connection in its header, or use the one under Settings → Nerd → Diagnostics. It goes through every step and shows each with its time: the name lookup (DNS), the connection, TLS, the login – with the account's end date and connections – and a live channel's first bytes and speed, against what SD, HD, Full HD and 4K need.

The stream steps use one of the account's connections for a few seconds. Copy gives you the result without logins, addresses or MAC addresses, ready to paste into a question to your provider or to us.
help_start_linux_q: How do I install it on Linux?
help_start_linux_a:
Three formats, all self-contained — Python, Qt, libmpv and ffmpeg are inside the download, so there is nothing to install alongside it.

AppImage — the one to take if you are not sure. It runs on any distribution:

chmod +x dopeIPTV-*.AppImage
./dopeIPTV-*.AppImage

.deb on Debian or Ubuntu:

sudo apt install ./dopeiptv_*_amd64.deb

Flatpak:

flatpak install --user dopeIPTV-*.flatpak

The AppImage and the .deb also come as arm64 builds, for a Raspberry Pi or an ARM server.

On Arch Linux, dopeIPTV is also in the AUR as dopeiptv. Install it with an AUR helper such as yay, and it updates along with the rest of the system:

yay -S dopeiptv
help_start_macos_q: How do I install it on macOS?
help_start_macos_a:
Open the .dmg and drag dopeIPTV to Applications. There is one for Apple Silicon, which needs macOS 15 or later, and one for Intel Macs, which needs macOS 14 or later.

The app is signed by Solecraft AB and notarised by Apple, so it opens like any other app. macOS only asks once whether you want to open an app downloaded from the internet.
help_start_windows_q: How do I install it on Windows?
help_start_windows_a:
Download the installer (dopeIPTV-*-windows-x64-setup.exe) and run it. It installs for your own user, with no admin rights, and adds dopeIPTV to the Start menu and to Settings → Apps, where you can also uninstall it — uninstalling removes everything dopeIPTV kept except your recordings.

Rather have nothing installed? The portable zip works as before: unzip it anywhere and run dopeiptv.exe. Settings → Advanced → Create shortcut adds a shortcut, and the README.txt in the zip lists everything to delete to remove it without a trace.

There is a native arm64 build for Snapdragon laptops; the x64 one also runs there under emulation, just slower.
help_start_playlist_q: How do I connect my provider?
help_start_playlist_a:
On first launch you pick what you have — most often an Xtream Codes account, which needs three things:

  • Server — the address with the port, like http://example.com:8080. Not a full playlist URL, just the host.
  • Username and Password — the ones your provider gave you.

They are saved. To add another account later, or edit this one: Settings → Sources. You can switch between playlists while the app is running, and favourites and history are kept separately for each.

Got an M3U address, or a portal address with a MAC address, instead? See the next two answers.
help_start_m3u_q: Can I use an M3U playlist instead?
help_start_m3u_a:
Yes. Choose M3U when adding a playlist and paste the URL your provider gave you.

An Xtream account gets more out of the app — catch-up, account expiry, the provider's own guide — because those come from an API an M3U list does not have. An M3U list plays and can be given its own XMLTV guide address, which covers most of the gap.
help_start_stalker_q: My provider gave me a portal address and a MAC address
help_start_stalker_a:
That is a Stalker / Ministra portal. When adding a playlist, choose Stalker / Ministra portal as the type, paste the portal address and enter the MAC address your provider registered, like 00:1A:79:12:34:56.

Channels, films, series and the guide's now and next work, and so does the portal's catch-up: a channel with an archive gets the ⏪ marker, and Timeshift / catch-up in its right-click menu, the ⏪ button in the player or a past programme in the guide plays a programme from its start — the next one follows when it ends. Portal support is still experimental.
help_start_pvr_q: A VDR, DVBViewer, NextPVR or MythTV server at home
help_start_pvr_a:
Each one is a source of its own. Settings → Sources → Add…, choose it under Type and type the server's address — or press Find on my network. An address without a port gets the usual one.

  • VDR — through two of its plugins: restfulapi (port 8002) for the channels with their groups and logos, the guide and the recordings, and streamdev-server (port 3000) for the streams. With streamdev alone the channels play, but there is no guide.
  • DVBViewer Media Server — port 8089, with its user name and password if it has one: channels and favourites, the guide and the recordings. The streams come from its port 7522.
  • NextPVR — port 8866 and its PIN, 0000 unless you changed it: channels and groups, the guide and the recordings.
  • MythTV — port 6544: the guide and the recordings. MythTV gives live TV only to its own frontends, so its channels are listed but do not play.

The recordings are under Movies, in Recordings on the box. Right-click a programme in the guide → Record on the box and the server records it.
help_start_satip_q: A SAT>IP server, or a Fritz!Box Cable
help_start_satip_a:
It is a source of its own: Settings → Sources → Add…, choose SAT>IP server under Type and press Find on my network, or type its address. That covers a Fritz!Box Cable, Digital Devices' Octopus NET, Telestar's Digibit, Kathrein's EXIP, minisatip and Tvheadend's SAT>IP server.

The channels come from the server's own list — a Fritz!Box's as HD channels, SD channels and Radio stations. A server without one needs a Channel list: an M3U of SAT>IP addresses, as a file or a web address. Such lists are published for each satellite and cable network.

Channels play over RTSP over TCP, which holds up on Wi-Fi too. On the source's Streams tab, set Streams over to RTSP over UDP for a server that takes no TCP, or to HTTP where the server streams over it too — then the rewind buffer can hold the channel.

Each channel takes one of the server's tuners while it plays. Before a multiview window, a recording or a cast would need one more than it has, the app asks first; Tuners to use leaves some for other TVs at home. SAT>IP sends no programme guide, so give the source an XMLTV address on its Guide tab.
help_start_media_q: A Jellyfin, Emby or Plex server
help_start_media_a:
Each one is a source of its own, with the server's films, series and artwork. Settings → Sources → Add… and choose it under Type.

  • Jellyfin and Emby — type the server's address (port 8096) or press Find on my network, then Sign in with your user name and password. The password is sent once and never kept. On Jellyfin, Use Quick Connect shows a code to enter in a Jellyfin app where you are signed in already.
  • Plex — Sign in with Plex opens Plex in your browser. Sign in there, then pick the Server from your account.

What you watch is told to the server, so its resume points and watched marks follow you, and what you were watching elsewhere shows under Continue watching; private viewing tells it nothing. Live TV and its guide come along where the server has them — on Plex that needs a tuner and Plex Pass on the server.
help_start_demo_q: Can I try it without an account?
help_start_demo_a: Yes. The setup wizard offers demo channels: a handful of free, public test streams from Mux, Apple and Bitmovin, so you can see the app work before typing anything in. They are official test assets, not anybody's TV service, and you can switch to a real playlist whenever you like.
help_start_newpc_q: Can I bring my settings to a new computer?
help_start_newpc_a:
Yes. When dopeIPTV starts for the first time, the setup wizard offers Already use dopeIPTV on another computer? Bring your settings. Type the sync code from Settings → Sync on the other computer — press Start on this computer there first if it has no code yet — or choose Restore a backup… instead.

Your profiles and settings come over. Your sources and watch history come too when the other computer syncs them, and from then on this computer syncs them as well.

Everything is encrypted on the computer before it is sent, and dopeiptv.org keeps only bytes it cannot read. No account, no email.
help_start_update_q: How do I update to a new version?
help_start_update_a:
Your settings, playlists and favourites are kept whichever way you update. About dopeIPTV, under Help (in the dopeIPTV menu on a Mac), shows which version you have, and so does the end of Settings → General.

AppImage — from 1.2.15 on it updates itself. When a new version is out, a banner in the app offers Update now, and so does About dopeIPTV: the app downloads the new version, checks it, test-starts it and swaps it in, then offers to restart. With an older AppImage, download the new one, make it executable, delete the old file and start the new one — the menu entry follows it.

.deb and Flatpak — install the new file the same way as the first time (by its full name if the old one is still in the folder). It replaces the old version.

AUR on Arch Linux — your AUR helper updates it along with the rest of the system, for example yay -Syu.

Windows — from 1.4.5 on, a copy installed with the installer updates itself: Update now in the banner or in About dopeIPTV downloads the new installer, shows its progress and opens the new version. With an older version, run the new installer. With the portable zip, close the app, delete the old dopeiptv folder and unzip the new one in its place.

macOS — from 1.4.5 on it updates itself the same way: Update now downloads the new version, checks that it is signed by Solecraft AB and notarised by Apple, and swaps it in when dopeIPTV restarts. The app has to be in Applications, not opened from the .dmg. With an older version, drag the new dopeIPTV to Applications and choose Replace.
help_watch_play_a:
Double-click it in the middle list, or press ▶ Play in the panel on the right. Picking another channel switches the stream in place rather than tearing the player down and building it again, which is what makes zapping quick.

In Movies, one click shows the film in the right-hand column — its plot, who is in it and, for one you have started, Continue with how far you got — and a double click or Enter plays it.

The Back and Next buttons in the player bar move through whatever list you are in — channels, a series' episodes, recordings or history.
help_watch_series_q: A series' page: seasons and episodes
help_watch_series_a:
Opening a series — from its list, Mine, Continue, New episodes or the command palette — shows its own page in place of the list: its picture, year, rating, genres and plot, and one button that plays on: Continue S2 E5 with how far you got, or Play S1 E1. Continue goes on from where you stopped, without asking. Beside it are Favorite, Follow and Watch later.

The seasons are in one row, Specials last, and the season you pick is remembered for the series. Its episodes are cards with their picture, length, plot, a watched check and a progress bar; the next one is marked Up next. One click picks an episode, and a double click or Enter plays it; one click plays only when Auto-play preview on selection is on under Settings → Playback, as in the lists. An episode plays in the player while the page stays, and autoplay moves it on to the next episode.

Back, Esc or the mouse's back button returns to the list just as you left it. On the keyboard, Up and Down move through the episodes, Left and Right through the seasons, and Enter plays; right-click an episode for its menu. Your own files' library has the same page, and TV mode's Series screen the same row of seasons.
help_watch_seek_q: How do I skip forward and back?
help_watch_seek_a:
For films, episodes, recordings and catch-up — anything with a known length:

  • Move the pointer over the picture and a scrubber slides up, with the timeline, the elapsed and total time, and −10s / +30s buttons.
  • Click the video once and use the arrow keys: a tap jumps ten seconds, holding one down seeks continuously.

Live channels have a rewind bar of their own — see the next answer.
help_watch_rewind_q: Can I pause and rewind live TV?
help_watch_rewind_a:
Yes, on any live channel. Move the pointer over the picture and a bar takes you back; pause and the arrow keys work too, and LIVE brings you back to now.

How far back is set under Settings → Playback → Rewind live channels: a couple of minutes in memory by default, or up to six hours with Keep the rewind buffer on disk.

Rewind with dopeIPTV's own buffer (experimental) goes further: the app keeps the channel itself on disk and goes on downloading while you pause, so LIVE never has to reconnect, and a channel you leave keeps its history until you close the app. On a channel with the provider's catch-up, DVR | TIMESHIFT at the left of the bar switches between this buffer and the archive.
help_watch_fullscreen_a:
Double-click the picture, or press F. Esc leaves it — and so does the explicit Exit fullscreen button in the floating control bar, which is there so nobody has to know about Esc.

The controls and the mouse pointer hide themselves after a few seconds of stillness and come back on the smallest movement.
help_watch_popout_q: Can I move the video to a second screen?
help_watch_popout_a:
Yes — pop the player out into its own window and drag it wherever you like.

It is frameless by default: drag anywhere on the picture to move it. Right-click for always-on-top, a title bar, or Exit. Esc also brings it home. The main window keeps working while it is out.
help_watch_tracks_q: Audio language, subtitles and picture settings
help_watch_tracks_a:
The ⚙ button in the player bar — it is in the fullscreen controls too — holds everything about the stream you are watching:

  • Audio track and subtitle track
  • Audio delay, when the sound is out of step
  • Aspect ratio (16:9, 4:3, stretch and so on)
  • Network buffer size
  • Stats for nerds: codecs, resolution, frame rate, hardware decoding, A/V sync, dropped frames, cache and network speed, live over the picture

A track you pick is remembered, and for a series it carries over to the next episode. To set a preference for every stream instead, see Settings below.
help_watch_teletext_a:
Where a channel sends them, they are in the player's ⚙ menu under Subtitles, by language and page, like “Swedish - teletext 199”. Your subtitle language under Settings → Picture & sound picks the page by itself, and a page you choose is remembered for the channel. Teletext subtitles need an mpv built with libzvbi: the AppImage and the .deb have it, the Mac app does not — DVB subtitles work there.

To read teletext itself, press T while a live channel plays, or choose Teletext… in the View menu. Type a page number, use the arrows for the next page and subpage, and the colour keys for the page's links. The pages are read from dopeIPTV's own rewind buffer, so nothing opens a second connection to your account: turn on Settings → Playback → Rewind with dopeIPTV's own buffer first.
help_watch_night_a:
Night mode tames the loud moments: loud adverts, explosions and bangs come down, while ordinary speech stays exactly as it is. It never makes anything louder, so the news sounds the same with it on. Press N, or choose Night mode in the player's ⚙ menu or under Settings → Playback.

It turns on at once while the stream plays on, stays on when you change channel, and is remembered for the next time. Whichever way you switch it, the app says so. If it cannot be turned on for a stream, the app tells you that instead.
help_watch_audio_q: Music and radio channels: the visualiser
help_watch_audio_a:
Some channels in a playlist send sound and no picture — a music or radio channel, say. Such a channel shows the visualiser you picked instead of a black picture.

To choose one, open the player's ⚙ menu → Visualiser. There are five styles: Bars, Spectrum, Waveform, Vectorscope and Frequencies.
help_watch_keys_a:
• Space — pause and resume
  • F — fullscreen, Esc to leave
  • ← / → — seek ten seconds, hold to keep going
  • M — mute

They work in the main window, in fullscreen and in the popped-out window alike. Settings → Keyboard shortcuts changes Space, F, M and the other single keys; the arrows stay as they are.
help_watch_search_q: How do I search all my sources at once?
help_watch_search_a:
Open Search among the places in the sidebar, or press Ctrl+Shift+F (⇧⌘F on a Mac). The guide's Search button opens it too, and so does the last row of the command palette, Search everywhere for “…”. Type something like Star Trek and every source is searched at once. The hits come in four groups — Channels, Programmes, Movies and Series — and each one names its source. Programmes are found on now and through the coming week, in the guides the app has already downloaded.

Enter or a double-click acts on a hit, and a right-click opens its menu. The results stay while a hit plays in the docked player, so you can try another.

  • A channel, or a programme on now, from another source plays without switching to that source.
  • A programme later: Enter sets a reminder, and the menu offers Record this programme.
  • A movie or a series from another source switches to that source first. Back from a series' page comes back to the results.

A Stalker portal is searched only in the lists it has already loaded, and the page says so. What your lists hide or lock is never shown, a kids profile finds nothing for adults, and during private viewing nothing is kept once you leave the page. Searching itself opens no stream.
help_watch_palette_q: Is there a quick way to find an action, a setting or a channel?
help_watch_palette_a:
Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) anywhere in the window and start typing. The command palette finds the app's actions with their keys, every setting, and the channels and programmes of the source you are using.

Up and Down choose, Enter runs it: a channel plays, a setting opens on its page, and a programme offers play, record or remind. Esc closes it. The key itself can be changed under Settings → Keyboard shortcuts.
help_watch_resume_q: Does it remember where I stopped?
help_watch_resume_a:
Yes, for films, series episodes, recordings and your own local files. Starting one again asks whether to resume at that point or start from the beginning; on a series' page, Continue goes straight on.

Positions very close to the start or the end are ignored on purpose, so it does not offer to resume something you had only just begun or had actually finished.
help_watch_stats_a:
Your statistics… in the History menu shows the time you watched this week, month and year, by day of the week and by hour, the channels, films and series you watch most, and your longest streak.

It is counted on this computer only and never sent anywhere, and each profile has its own. Private viewing adds nothing, and Clear recent history clears it too.
help_watch_web_q: Can I play YouTube or Twitch?
help_watch_web_a:
Yes, live streams and videos from YouTube, Twitch and sites like them. Choose Open address… in the File menu or press Ctrl+L (⌘L on a Mac), paste the page's address and press Play. Tick Save to favorites to keep it with your favourites, marked LIVE while it is live.

These pages play through yt-dlp. If your system has none, the app offers to download the official release from GitHub — about 35 MB, checked against its checksum, kept in the app's own folder and updated as it is used. Settings → Playback shows which yt-dlp is in use and has Update now; turn off Keep an up-to-date copy of yt-dlp for the app to use only the one your system has.
help_watch_tvmode_a:
A full-screen layout of its own for watching on the TV from the sofa, run with a remote. Turn it on with TV mode in the View menu or Ctrl+Shift+T. Start in TV mode under Settings → General opens it every time the app starts; dopeiptv --tv does it once.

Along the top are Home, Channels, Guide, Movies, Series, Search and Options. The arrows move, OK plays or opens, and Back goes back a step. Over the picture, up and down change the channel, and typing a number goes straight to one.

Back over the picture takes you to the menus while the stream goes on: what plays is shown above the tabs, and OK on it, Play or Back brings the picture back. Stop stops it. Leave TV mode under Options.

Options also records what you are watching: press Record, and a small REC sits in the corner of the picture while it runs. It records from what already plays, so it needs no second connection to your provider; the same tile stops it.
help_watch_tvremote_q: Which remote works in TV mode?
help_watch_tvremote_a:
A remote that acts as a keyboard always works — most USB and Bluetooth ones do — and so does the TV's own remote over HDMI-CEC once the system turns its buttons into keys. On Linux, TV mode also reads a game controller and LIRC; turn off Read game controllers and LIRC under Settings → General if a remote's keys arrive twice. Your phone can be the remote too — see the next answer.

The colour keys do the same everywhere: red adds a channel to your favourites or takes it away, green opens the guide, yellow search and blue the options. On a keyboard: the arrows, Enter for OK, Esc for Back, Space to pause, X to stop and F1–F4 for the colour keys.
help_watch_phone_q: Can I use my phone as a remote?
help_watch_phone_a:
Yes. Choose Phone remote… in the View menu, press Turn on and scan the code with the phone's camera. A page opens in its browser, with nothing to install: what is on, your channels and favourites with a search, play and pause, channel up and down, and the volume.

While TV mode is on, the page becomes a remote: arrows and OK, Back, Options, the colour keys, volume and channel, and number keys — or a touchpad, where a swipe moves, a tap is OK and a long press is Back. When you have gone back to the menus, tap the Now playing card — Show on TV — to bring the picture back. The TV mode button at the top of the page turns TV mode on and off.

While a live channel plays, Now playing shows how far back the rewind buffer reaches: drag the bar to go back — it shows how far behind live you will be —, skip with the buttons, and Live brings you back to now. More opens Subtitles and sound, the Sleep timer and Record, which asks before it starts.

The remote stays on, also after the app restarts, until you press Stop.
help_watch_phonehome_q: Can I put the remote on my phone's home screen?
help_watch_phonehome_a:
Yes. It then opens like an app, as dopeIPTV Remote with dopeIPTV's icon and no address bar. With the remote's page open:

  • iPhone — in Safari, tap Share → Add to Home Screen.
  • Android — in Chrome, open the ⋮ menu → Add to home screen.

New address in the app's Phone remote window shuts out every phone that had the old address, and the icon on the home screen stops working too: scan the new code and add it again.

The remote answers only on your home network, never from the internet. A phone on another part of it — a guest network, say — works too when the router lets it through to this computer.
help_tv_epg_q: Where does the programme guide come from?
help_tv_epg_a:
From your provider. Every live channel in the list shows what is on now with a progress bar, and the detail panel shows what is next.

The guide is cached on disk for each playlist, so it is on screen the moment you start the app — the fresh copy downloads in the background and replaces it. If that download fails, the cached guide stays rather than leaving you with nothing.
help_tv_guide_a:
Yes. Guide among the places opens a programme grid of the category you are in, with a timeline you can scroll through. Pick another category in the sidebar — a folder of favourite channels too — and the guide follows it. A double-click on a category opens its guide, and a double-click on it again goes back to its list. The guide's Search button opens the Search page, which finds a programme in the guides of all your sources — see How do I search all my sources at once?

The rows are low, so many channels fit on the screen. A programme on now has a thin strip that shows how far it has got. For a line through the whole guide at the time now, turn on Line at the time now under Settings → Guide.

Drag the edge of the channel column to make it wider or narrower, and double-click the edge to put it back. When the column is narrow, only the logos show — point at one to see the channel's name. Entries such as “-= Sweden =-” become headings, and a channel without guide data has an empty row.

On a channel with catch-up, double-clicking a programme that has already aired plays it from the archive.
help_tv_xmltv_q: The guide is wrong, empty, or for the wrong country
help_tv_xmltv_a:
Give that playlist its own guide instead of the provider's:

  1. Settings → Sources
  2. Open the source's own page: its ›, or a double-click
  3. On its Guide tab, put an XMLTV address in Custom TV guide URL

It replaces whatever the provider sends. The app matches your channels to that guide by EPG id first and by channel name second, so a guide from a different source usually still lines up.
help_tv_times_q: Everything is shifted by an hour or two
help_tv_times_a:
Some providers publish times that do not match what they actually broadcast. Two separate corrections live in Settings → Guide:

  • EPG delay shifts every time the guide displays.
  • Replay delay shifts where catch-up and timeshift start playing, without touching the listings.

They are separate because providers get these two wrong independently of each other.
help_tv_ts_a:
Some providers keep a recording of each channel for a few days. Where yours does, the channel gets a ⏪ marker in the list, and the detail panel says how many days deep the archive goes.

If a channel has no marker, the provider is not offering an archive for it. That is their setting and nothing in the app can turn it on.
help_tv_tsstart_q: How do I watch something that already started?
help_tv_tsstart_a:
Press the ⏪ button in the player — it is in the fullscreen controls too — or right-click the channel and choose Timeshift. Then pick from the start.

What plays is a piece of the archive, so it seeks like a film: the scrubber and the arrow keys both work inside it.
help_tv_tsbrowse_q: Can I go back to yesterday?
help_tv_tsbrowse_a:
Yes. The timeshift menu lists past programmes grouped by day — double-click one to watch it. You can also jump back in fixed steps, and those steps scale to how deep your provider's archive actually is, from thirty minutes up to a week.

Some providers accept an archive request and quietly serve the live feed instead. The app checks and tells you when that happens rather than letting you think you are watching yesterday.
help_tv_rec_a:
Several ways in:

  • The REC button in the player, for what you are watching now.
  • Right-click any channel → Record, for one you are not watching.
  • In TV mode, Options → Record.
  • On the phone remote, More → Record.

Unless you choose a length it records until you stop it. While it runs, it stays at the foot of the sidebar with its time: click it to stop — the app asks first, and what has been recorded so far is kept. With two at once you pick which one. You can watch a recording while it is still being written.

While you pause, a recording taken from the player's stream stands still as well, and the app tells you so. With dopeIPTV's own buffer turned on, Record records from the buffer instead: whole while you pause, and from where you are when you have gone back.
help_tv_recwhen_q: Can I set a length, or schedule one?
help_tv_recwhen_a:
Yes to both. The REC menu offers 30 minutes, 1, 2 or 4 hours, and a scheduled recording takes a start and a stop time.

Scheduled jobs survive restarting the app, but the app has to be running when they fire — it is a program, not a background service. Recordings → Active & scheduled shows what is pending.
help_tv_reconn_q: Will recording use up my second connection?
help_tv_reconn_a:
Not if you record the channel you are watching: that taps the player's own stream, so it costs nothing extra and works on the usual accounts that allow only one stream at a time.

Recording a different channel, or a scheduled job starting later, does open its own connection to the provider.

One thing to know about an in-player recording: it is finalised when the recording stops, so stopping playback, zapping to another channel or a stream error ends it.
help_tv_reccap_q: Can I stop a recording filling the disk?
help_tv_reccap_a: Yes, at two levels. Settings → Recording takes a size limit that applies to every recording — a number plus MB, GB or TB. And the player's REC menu has a quick limit for the current session only, from 250 MB to 10 GB.
help_tv_recwhere_a:
Wherever you set under Settings → Recording. Recordings among the places shows them with a picture from each and how far you watched, grouped by day — Today, Yesterday, Earlier this week, Last week, then by month — with what records now and next at the top.

The sort button puts them oldest first, by name, under their channels, the longest or the largest first, and Unwatched only at the foot of its menu hides what you have seen. Subfolders are categories: create folders, rename, move things between them, and select several to delete at once.
help_more_title: Multiview, casting, home server, Trakt and Simkl
help_more_mv_a:
A separate window showing 2, 4, 6 or 9 live channels at once in a grid, each one an independent stream. They can come from different playlists and even different accounts.

Open it from the View menu, or right-click a channel → Add to multiview; the grid size is under Settings → Multiview. Double-click a window to maximise it.
help_more_mvaudio_q: Which window do I hear, and how do I change one?
help_more_mvaudio_a:
Click a window to give it the audio — a red border marks the one you are hearing.

Right-click any window for: mute, audio and subtitle track, move or swap it with another, or remove it. A channel with catch-up gets its own archive timeline inside its window, so you can rewind one channel while the others stay live.
help_more_mvcost_q: Why does multiview say it will use several connections?
help_more_mvcost_a:
Because it does — one per window. Most IPTV accounts allow only one or two streams at a time, so a nine-window grid will simply be refused by most providers.

The app says this once, before you find out from a wall of failing streams. If you see “connection limit reached”, this is usually why.
help_more_cast_q: How do I cast to a TV or a Chromecast?
help_more_cast_a:
Right-click a channel, film or episode → Cast to TV…, then pick the device. Chromecasts, smart TVs and Kodi are in the same list: a TV that speaks DLNA/UPnP — Samsung, LG, Sony, Philips, Panasonic and many others — is marked (DLNA), and Kodi (Kodi). A Chromecast gets live channels as HLS, which is what a Cast receiver expects; a TV fetches the stream as it is.

Casting stops local playback — the two would be a second connection to your provider. A card takes the video's place: what plays, on which TV and how it is going, with pause, 30 seconds back and forward, volume, tracks and Stop. A TV that gets stuck buffering is sent the stream again by itself, twice, and then the card offers Try again. While it casts, a channel, film or episode you pick goes to the same device; only stopping the cast ends it. A device the search does not find is added with Add a device by address… in the same window.
help_more_castfix_a:
Some channels are ordinary H.264 video with Dolby Digital Plus audio. A Chromecast that is not an Ultra or a Google TV has no decoder for that and rejects the stream without saying why.

The app converts those on this computer and serves the result on your own network: the video is copied through untouched — only the audio is re-encoded, which is cheap — and it only happens after the device has actually refused the stream. A channel your device can play always gets the provider's own stream, unaltered.

This needs ffmpeg, which is inside every packaged download.
help_more_castback_q: Can I go back while casting a live channel?
help_more_castback_a:
Yes, with the timeshift button or the timeline on the cast card. A channel with the provider's catch-up goes back in the archive, as far as the provider keeps it.

dopeIPTV's own rewind buffer works too. A cast started from a moment in the buffer plays from it. To go back in the buffer while the TV plays live, the buffer has to go on recording beside the cast: turn on Settings → Casting → Keep the rewind buffer while casting. It is off by default because it uses one more connection to your provider, and most accounts allow only one — turn it on only if yours allows more. When the limit is full or not known, the app asks first.

A DLNA TV or a Kodi goes back in the archive only. On an Apple TV a channel plays live — going back is not offered there.
help_more_appletv_q: Can I cast to an Apple TV?
help_more_appletv_a:
From a Mac, yes: in Cast to TV…, pick AirPlay and press Cast. A small AirPlay window opens — click the AirPlay button in it and choose your Apple TV.

On the Apple TV a channel plays live — going back is not offered there — while films and episodes pause and seek as usual. The Apple TV's own remote sets the volume.

From Linux or Windows, no. AirPlay to an Apple TV needs Apple's own frameworks, which only macOS has, and since tvOS 18 an Apple TV takes no video from other senders. What works instead:

  • Cast to a Chromecast, a DLNA TV or Kodi.
  • Let the Apple TV watch through dopeIPTV's Server for the home — see the next answer: the Plex or Jellyfin app, once your Plex or Jellyfin server has dopeIPTV as its tuner, or an IPTV app such as VLC or iPlayTV with the server's playlist.

Share channels and guide, under Settings → Nerd → Remote and automation with Reachable from set to My home network too, also gives such an app a playlist and a guide, but the app then fetches each channel from your provider itself — one more connection.
help_more_server_q: Can other devices at home watch through dopeIPTV?
help_more_server_a:
Yes: dopeIPTV can be the home's server as well as its player. With Nerd on, turn on Serve my channels to the home network under Settings → Nerd → Remote and automation → Server for the home. It is off by default.

  • Plex, Jellyfin and Emby find it by themselves as an HDHomeRun tuner when you set up live TV in them. If one does not, give it the address from Copy the tuner's address. For the guide, give them the XMLTV address on the server's page.
  • VLC, Kodi or a TV's IPTV app: paste the address from Copy the playlist's address. The playlist carries the guide's address.

Each channel is fetched from your provider once and shared by everyone watching it — the app's own player too — and never more channels at once than your account allows. Your own viewing and recordings in the app always come first, and a device that would need one more connection is told that all tuners are in use. Most accounts allow one connection, and then everyone watches the same channel.

Only devices on your home network get in. Open in the browser shows the server's page: who watches what, the addresses, and its few settings — the port, how many channels at once, and which sources and categories it serves. Hidden and locked categories are never served; adult ones only with Channels for adults turned on.

If the port is in use, the app says whether dopeIPTV's own server holds it — a dopeiptv --server started earlier, for example — or another program, and offers the next free port: one click, and the server starts there.
help_more_headless_q: Can it run on a NAS or a Raspberry Pi without a screen?
help_more_headless_a:
Yes. dopeiptv --server runs the same server without a window. It serves the sources and settings dopeIPTV has on that computer and prints the address of the server's page. Like the server in the window, it keeps the guides current by itself: each source's guide is downloaded again once its copy is six hours old. Ctrl+C stops it.

  • --port and a number listens on that port this time; the setting stays as it is.
  • --no-discovery leaves UDP port 65001 alone, for when another tuner emulator on the computer answers there. Plex, Jellyfin and Emby then need the tuner's address.

The server's page shows the command. To have it running day and night, start it with the computer: a systemd user service on Linux, a login item on macOS, Task Scheduler on Windows. Run either this or the server in the app's window, not both. A server without a window does not know what dopeIPTV plays on another computer — to it, that is another device on your account.
help_more_together_q: Can I watch together with friends?
help_more_together_a:
Yes. Choose Watch together… in the View menu, type the name the others will see and press Start a room. Share the code you get, like K7PQ-M2XD; the others type it and press Join. A room holds up to eight people.

Each of you plays from your own source, so it takes no extra connection: when one of you starts, pauses or skips, the others follow in step. A film or an episode is found in each source by its title, and if a source does not have it, the others go on watching. A live channel is only tuned to, so you may be a few seconds apart. Your own files and recordings cannot be shared.

What the room sends is encrypted with a key made from the code; dopeiptv.org only passes it on and cannot see your names or what you watch. Watch together is off during private viewing, and it is only in the official app.
help_more_subs_q: How do I get subtitles for a film or an episode?
help_more_subs_a:
While it plays, open the player's Subtitles menu → Find subtitles online…. The app searches OpenSubtitles.com for what you are watching, in your subtitle language, and lists the matches — one made for exactly that file first. Pick one and it shows straight away; the next time you play the title it comes back by itself.

If the app asks for an API key: sign in at opensubtitles.com, open API consumers, create a key and enter it under Settings → Integrations. Signing in with your OpenSubtitles account there is optional and raises how many subtitles you can download a day. A subtitle file you already have loads with Load subtitle file… in the same menu.

How many: without an account, OpenSubtitles lets each internet connection download 5 subtitles a day; with a free account entered under Settings → Integrations, 20 a day. Searching never counts, and a subtitle you have downloaded stays on your computer, so playing it again costs nothing. When the day's downloads are used up, the app says so — try again the next day.
help_more_trakt_a:
Settings → Watch history → Connect via browser. Your browser opens Trakt: sign in if you are not already, click Yes, and the app is connected. There are no keys to create and no code to type.

After that, what you watch is scrobbled, and your watchlist and history can be browsed inside the app. Your own local files are scrobbled too, whenever TMDB could identify the file.
help_more_simkl_a:
Settings → Watch history → Connect with a code, under Simkl. The app shows a short code and opens simkl.com/pin in your browser: sign in there, type the code, and the app is connected.

Simkl keeps track of what you watch, as Trakt does — use one of them, or both side by side. The films and episodes you play are scrobbled, what you mark as watched or for later in the app goes there too, and what you have watched there shows as watched here. Its watchlist and history can be browsed in the app. Live TV and recordings are not sent. Each profile connects its own account.
help_local_add_q: Can I watch my own files?
help_local_add_a:
Yes. Local files in the sidebar browses folders you add under Settings → Local files.

A network share your system has already mounted appears by itself — a gvfs SMB mount on Linux, a share under /Volumes on macOS, a mapped drive on Windows. These are ordinary paths as far as the app is concerned, so there is no SMB client inside it to misbehave.
help_local_views_a:
Both, switched in the place's header.

  • Folders shows the tree exactly as it is on disk.
  • Library reads the file names and builds series with seasons and episodes out of them, with films under Movies — the same shape as the provider's own sections.

The sort button orders every folder: by name A→Z or Z→A, last modified, oldest, largest or by type — folders always first. A file that is added, renamed or removed shows by itself; a network share is looked at again every few minutes, and Rescan (F5) does it at once.
help_local_art_q: Where do the posters come from?
help_local_art_a:
TMDB, for anything that can be matched by name and year. What cannot be matched gets a frame grabbed from the video itself, and music gets its cover from the file's tags or a cover image in the folder.

A file with no year and no release tag in its name is never guessed at. That is deliberate: a wrong poster is worse than a thumbnail. Rename the file to include the year if you want it matched.
help_local_music_a:
Yes. Albums are shelved together, artist, album and title come from the tags, and there is a play queue: add a track, queue a whole folder, or play something next. It moves to the next track by itself when one ends.

There is also a visualiser and a ten-band equaliser.
help_local_radio_q: Can I listen to internet radio?
help_local_radio_a:
Yes. Radio in the sidebar, under Local files, browses the stations of radio-browser.info: Most voted, Most listened, a search of all stations, and lists by country, language and genre. A station plays with the visualiser and equaliser, and shows what the station says is on now.

Right-click a station to add it to My stations; your stations are there in every source. The app tells radio-browser.info which stations you play only if you turn on Tell radio-browser.info which stations I play under Settings → Integrations.
help_local_missing_q: A file in History will not play
help_local_missing_a:
It has been moved, renamed, or its share is not mounted. History says which, and offers to remove the entry, instead of failing silently.

If it is a share, mount it and try again — the entry will work as it did before.
help_set_language_a:
Settings → General. The interface is translated into 27 languages and switches immediately, with no restart. Arabic, Persian, Hebrew and Urdu mirror the entire layout.

Settings → Appearance: themes, light and dark, picked from small pictures of the app; an accent colour, or any colour you like; following the desktop's light and dark mode; corner style and the size of text and controls — all applied live.
help_set_playback_a:
Settings → Playback and Picture & sound set what should happen without you asking each time:

  • Preferred audio language
  • Subtitles on or off, with a first and second preferred language
  • Default aspect ratio and network buffer
  • How early the “Next episode” card appears — off, or from 10 seconds to ten minutes

The ⚙ menu in the player still overrides any of these for the stream you are watching.

How far back live channels can be rewound is set on the Playback page too.
help_set_parental_q: Can I lock things away from other people?
help_set_parental_a:
Yes. A PIN protects locked categories and locked favourite groups. A locked group does not reveal which channels are in it until the PIN is entered — hiding the contents, not just the playback.

The PIN is stored salted and hashed, not in plain text.
help_set_profiles_q: Can everyone in the house have their own profile?
help_set_profiles_a:
Yes. Settings → Profiles → Add a profile — up to eight, each with a name, a colour or an emoji, and a four-digit PIN if you want one. With two or more, the avatar at the foot of the sidebar shows who is watching; click it to switch. What plays stops, and the other person's things are there at once, with no restart.

Ask who's watching puts “Who's watching?” on screen as the app starts. A profile with a PIN always asks for it.

Each profile keeps its own favourites, history and Continue watching, Watch later, watched marks, followed series, reminders, statistics, Trakt and Simkl, what the places show, theme and accent, and audio and subtitle languages. Sources, recordings, the guide, devices, playback and network settings, Nerd and the parental lock are shared. In Settings, a profile's own rows are marked This profile's.

A kids profile sees only what the parental lock leaves open, is never asked for a PIN for the rest, and opens Settings only with a grown-up's PIN.
help_set_sync_q: The same favourites and settings on all my computers
help_set_sync_a:
Settings → Sync → Start on this computer gives you a sync code. On your other computers, choose Join with a code… and type it; a new computer can take it in the setup wizard — see Can I bring my settings to a new computer? From then on your favourites and settings are the same everywhere — and, if you tick them, your playlists with their logins and your watch history. Keyboard shortcuts sync only between computers of the same system: Mac with Mac, Windows with Windows, Linux with Linux. A change syncs half a minute later.

It is free for everyone, with no supporter key. Everything is encrypted on your computer with a key made from the code before it is sent; dopeiptv.org keeps only the encrypted bytes, under a random number, and cannot read them. No account, no email, no name. A copy no computer has synced for 180 days is deleted. Sync is only in the official app.
help_set_hide_q: Can I hide or rename channels?
help_set_hide_a:
Right-click any channel, film or series to rename or hide it. The result is effectively your own edited playlist, saved per playlist, and Restore default channels… puts everything back exactly as the provider sends it.

Whole categories can be hidden, renamed or locked from the category right-click menu. A hidden category's channels are left out of “All” as well.
help_set_bouquets_q: Can I edit my Enigma2 box's channel lists?
help_set_bouquets_a:
Yes, on a VU+, Dreambox, Zgemma or any box with OpenWebif that is one of your sources: right-click one of its channels → The box → Edit the box's channel lists….

Make, rename, move and delete TV and radio bouquets. In a bouquet, drag the channels into order (or Ctrl+↑ / Ctrl+↓), rename with F2, remove with Delete, and add markers and spacers. Add channels takes them from all the box's channels, or a satellite's or a provider's, with a search.

Each change goes straight to the box, in the order you make it. Before the first one, the box backs up every list. Under Backup, Save the backup… keeps a copy on your computer, Undo this window's changes… puts the lists back as they were, and Restore a backup from a file… puts a saved one back. When the window closes, the app reads the new order in. What is playing is left alone.

It needs OpenWebif's bouquet editor. An older OpenWebif or the Dreambox WebInterface has none: update OpenWebif from the box's plugin list. A kids profile cannot edit the lists.
help_set_playlists_a:
Add as many as you like under Settings → Sources and switch between them while the app runs. Each one keeps its own favourites, history, hidden channels and renames.

The button with your source's initials at the foot of the sidebar switches to another. While something plays from another source, the line under the list says which.

Each one also has a page of its own — its ›, or a double-click — with its own XMLTV guide address on the Guide tab, and on Advanced how often it refreshes: never, at startup, every 2, 6 or 12 hours, daily or weekly.
help_set_testbuilds_q: Can I try the next version early?
help_set_testbuilds_a:
Yes. Settings → General → Update channel → Test builds offers each test build of the next version as soon as it is made, in the same update banner — and on the AppImage with the same one-click update. Test builds can have faults a release does not.

Back on Releases, you keep the test build until the next release comes out.
help_fix_logs_q: How do I get a log?
help_fix_logs_a:
The log is what turns “it does not work” into something fixable, and credentials are masked out of it automatically, so it is safe to attach to an issue.

Run the app from a terminal with DOPEIPTV_LOG_FILE set and it writes one there as well as to the screen.

Linux — AppImage

DOPEIPTV_LOG_FILE=/tmp/dopeiptv.log ./dopeIPTV-*.AppImage

Linux — .deb or pipx

DOPEIPTV_LOG_FILE=/tmp/dopeiptv.log dopeiptv

macOS

DOPEIPTV_LOG_FILE=/tmp/dopeiptv.log \
  /Applications/dopeIPTV.app/Contents/MacOS/dopeiptv

Windows — PowerShell, in the unzipped folder, or for an installed copy in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\dopeIPTV

$env:DOPEIPTV_LOG_FILE="$env:TEMP\dopeiptv.log"
.\dopeiptv.exe

Reproduce the problem, close the app, and attach the file. For much more detail add DOPEIPTV_LOG=debug in front of the same command.
help_fix_start_a:
Start it from a terminal — see the answer above for the exact command on your system — and read what it prints. That names the cause far more often than not.

The packaged builds carry everything they need. If you installed from source with pipx you also need mpv and ffmpeg from your distribution:

sudo apt install mpv ffmpeg     # Debian/Ubuntu
sudo dnf install mpv ffmpeg     # Fedora
sudo pacman -S mpv ffmpeg       # Arch
help_fix_picture_q: Sound plays but there is no picture
help_fix_picture_a:
The embedded player is not getting a video surface.

  1. Open ⚙ → Stats for nerds and see whether frames are arriving at all — that separates a stream problem from a display one.
  2. On Wayland, try Settings → Advanced → Run via X11 backend and restart the app.
  3. Run from a terminal and look for lines mentioning GL or mpv.

A music or radio channel may send sound and no picture at all. It then shows the visualiser — see Music and radio channels: the visualiser.
help_fix_gatekeeper_q: macOS says the app cannot be opened
help_fix_gatekeeper_a:
The version on this site is notarised by Apple and opens directly. An older download is not: open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down to the note about dopeIPTV and click Open Anyway, then confirm with your password.

If macOS instead says the app is “damaged”, that is the quarantine flag from the download. Clear it in Terminal:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/dopeIPTV.app
help_fix_smartscreen_a: SmartScreen does not recognise the publisher yet, because the installer and the app are not code-signed. Click More info, then Run anyway. It asks only the first time: updates from inside the app do not.
help_fix_defender_a:
A false positive. Two of its causes were fixed in 1.2.10: the launcher is now compiled from source instead of being the stock prebuilt one that antivirus engines hold signatures for, and the executable carries a proper version resource.

If your engine still flags it, allow the folder in your antivirus and report the false positive to Microsoft — that is what eventually clears it for everybody, not just for you.
help_fix_stream_a:
The app probes the provider and tells you why in plain language rather than showing a bare failure: account expired, connection limit reached, stream missing, server unreachable, and so on.

If other channels play, it is that channel. If nothing plays, check Settings → Sources — the account panel shows the expiry date and how many connections the account allows.
help_fix_loading_a:
That is the app waiting for your provider. While a channel starts, the picture shows a spinner with the channel's name, its logo when the app has it, and Connecting…. After 8 seconds it says Still loading - some channels take a while to start. Reconnecting… means a live stream dropped and the app is opening it again; Buffering… 45% means the stream stalled and is filling up again. A channel that starts at once never shows it.

Some channels simply take 10 or 15 seconds. If it stays much longer, or keeps coming back, the cause is at the provider or the account — see A channel will not play, “Connection limit reached” and The picture stutters and keeps jumping back. With Nerd on, Test connection on the source's page under Settings → Sources checks the way to the provider step by step.
help_fix_limit_a:
Your account allows a certain number of streams at the same time and they are all in use. In order of likelihood:

  1. Multiview is open — each window is a connection.
  2. A recording of a different channel is running.
  3. Another device or another person is using the account.
  4. A previous session has not timed out yet at the provider; waiting a minute often clears it.

Recording the channel you are watching does not count as a second connection.
help_fix_stutter_q: The picture stutters and keeps jumping back
help_fix_stutter_a:
The provider keeps cutting the stream — if this account is playing on another device or app, close it there.

Almost always the same account is playing somewhere else at the same time — a TV, a phone, another app, or someone you share it with. The provider allows only so many streams at once, so the two take turns: it cuts one off to let the other in, again and again.

Close the stream on the other device and the picture runs smoothly again. When every connection is taken before you even start, the app says so instead:

All 2/2 connections are in use — close the stream on your other device or app
help_fix_login_a:
Wrong username or password.

The provider turned the details down. It is almost always a slip when they were typed or copied:

  1. Username and password are case-sensitive.
  2. A space came along when you copied them — remove it at the start or end.
  3. The server address often needs its port, such as http://example.com:8080. Use exactly what your provider sent.
  4. Got an Xtream or M3U link? Paste the whole link into Server and the app fills in the rest.
  5. On a MAC portal the MAC address must be the one your provider registered.
help_fix_expired_a:
Your subscription has expired — renew it with your provider

The provider has ended the account, so nothing plays. Settings → Sources shows the expiry date. Renew with your provider and the playlist works again — there is nothing to add again in the app.

If the provider has disabled the account, the app says that too; only the provider can turn it back on.
help_fix_vpn_a:
The provider blocked this stream (HTTP 458) — usually anti-VPN/re-streaming, a connection limit, or a region/device block. Turn off any VPN and check with your provider.

Many providers turn away VPNs and data centres, since that is how accounts get resold. Turn the VPN off — or leave dopeIPTV outside it, if your VPN lets you choose apps — and try the channel again.

No VPN on? Then ask your provider: the account may be locked to one country, device or address.
help_fix_notstarted_q: An event channel will not play
help_fix_notstarted_a:
This stream hasn't started yet — it looks like an upcoming event. Try again once it's live.

Sports and pay-per-view channels are often empty until the event begins. Nothing is wrong with the account or the app — try again once it is live. The channel name usually says when it starts.
help_fix_vlan_q: “Find on my network” or the cast window finds nothing
help_fix_vlan_a:
A home network split into parts — VLANs, a guest or a gadget network — keeps a search on the part this computer is on. A box, a Chromecast or a TV on another part is not found unless the router passes the search on, and lets traffic through between the parts. What passes it on:

  • an mDNS reflector (Avahi's reflector, “Multicast DNS” on UniFi) — Chromecasts and Kodi
  • an SSDP relay or UPnP proxy — DLNA TVs
  • an IGMP proxy — multicast TV

Or tell the app where to look:

  • In the cast window, Add a device by address… adds a Chromecast, a TV or a Kodi by its address.
  • In Settings → Sources → Add…, type the box's address instead of searching.
  • With Nerd on, list the other parts under Settings → Nerd → Network → Other networks. “Find on my network” and the cast window then ask each address there directly.

The phone remote and the remote API accept every home address range, so a phone on another part of the network reaches them when the router allows it.
help_fix_icon_q: Linux: the taskbar shows a blank icon
help_fix_icon_a:
On Wayland, GNOME and KDE take a window's icon from a desktop entry matching it and ignore what the application sets for itself. An AppImage has no such entry until something installs one.

  1. The app offers to add one the first time it starts. Say yes — then restart the app, because the window you are looking at keeps the icon it opened with.
  2. The same switch is under Settings → General if you said no.
  3. If the icon still does not appear, a stale icon cache is hiding it. GTK reads that file instead of the folder:
rm ~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/icon-theme.cache

Installed from the .deb, the entry is already there and none of this applies.
help_fix_external_a:
That option launches a standalone mpv or vlc from your system, so one of them has to be installed — the built-in player needs nothing extra and is unaffected.

sudo apt install mpv vlc        # Debian/Ubuntu
sudo dnf install mpv vlc        # Fedora
sudo pacman -S mpv vlc          # Arch
nf_lede: The link may be out of date or mistyped. Start again from the front page, or look in the help.
hero_alt: dopeIPTV with the channel list and a channel playing, in five of its themes
feat_mine_p: Pick up where you left off, see the favourite channels you usually watch at this hour, keep a list of what to watch later and catch new episodes of the series you follow.
feat_tv_p: A full-screen layout made for the sofa, run with a remote, a game controller or your phone — which also rewinds live TV, records and picks the subtitles.
feat_room_p: Fold the places into a row of icons, take out the ones you never use, or turn on Just the list for nothing but your channels and films.
help_watch_places_q: Where is everything? The places in the sidebar
help_watch_places_a:
The sidebar starts with the places: Mine, TV, Movies, Series, Guide, Search, Local files, Radio and Recordings. Under them are the categories of the place you are in, and at its foot the button with your source's initials, which switches source and opens its settings.

Every place has the same calm header: the category's name, a filter, the sort button and, where it fits, Grid / List. The sort button's menu holds the orders the place has — for channels and films the provider's order, A→Z, Z→A and more, or As in all categories to follow the order chosen in Settings. How many there are, and which source the list comes from, is in the status line at the bottom.

The app opens where you left off. To start on Mine every time, choose it under Open on in Settings → General.
help_watch_mine_a:
Everything that is yours, from every source: Continue with what you were watching and how far you got, Your favorites, your favourite channels with what is on now — the ones you usually watch at this hour first, marked Usually watched now —, your list of what to watch later, New episodes of series you follow, and your History, day by day.

The field at the top searches everything you saved and watched, and the chips under it narrow it to channels, movies, series and the rest. In the list of what to watch later, Alt+Up and Alt+Down move a title and Delete takes it off; a title you watch to the end leaves it by itself. The Favorite folders tab keeps your own folders, if you like to sort things yourself.
help_set_room_q: Can I make more room for the list?
help_set_room_a:
Yes, under Settings → Appearance → What the places show:

  • Just the list takes away the rows over TV, Movies, Series and Local files and makes the headers smaller; Movies and Series show as rows and TV compact. Turned off again, everything is as you had it.
  • Rows over the lists picks the rows one by one — Recently watched, Continue, My stations, what records now and next. A row can also go from its heading's right-click menu: Hide this row.
  • In the sidebar takes out the places you never use: Guide, Search, Local files, Radio and Recordings. They still open from their shortcut, the command palette and the menus.
  • Fold the places — or the small arrow under them — turns the places into a row of icons, so the categories get the height.

These choices are each profile's own.

fl_mv_p: 2, 4, 6 or 9 live channels at once, from any of your sources.
fl_popout_p: The video in a window of its own, on top or on another screen.
fl_tracks_p: Pick the audio and subtitle track, set the delay and aspect ratio, and keep your defaults.
fl_night_p: Loud adverts and bangs brought down towards speech — never louder.
